title: How do we write three and three fourths as a fraction?
description: A mixed number is written as a regular fraction by turning each whole into fourths. The board writes each whole as four fourths, adds all the fourths and checks by taking the wholes back out. Keeko doubts the sum by adding the whole number to the top number.
teaching_notes: One idea: each whole unit is as many fractional units as the bottom number says. Watch for students who add the whole number straight onto the top number.

source: Can we write a mixed number as a regular fraction? Write 3 + 3/4 as a fraction.
video_script.why: A learner writes a mixed number as a regular fraction by turning each whole into fractional units.
video_script.substitution: the book's own mixed number three and three fourths
video_script.anchor: three whole unit bars and three fourth-unit bars on a number line from 0 to 4
video_script.wrong_answer: three plus three fourths is six fourths, because three and three make six
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the whole number to the top number, though each whole is four fourths.
video_script.payoff_line: Three plus three fourths is fifteen fourths

final_answer.spoken: yes, three plus three fourths is fifteen fourths

video_script.fraction_reading: one fourth, three fourths, four fourths, twelve fourths, fifteen fourths
video_script.design: Three whole bars each cut into four fourths, then three more fourths. All the fourths are counted together.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; three whole unit bars and a bar with three of four parts shaded, written as 3 + 3/4

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.bars: three whole unit bars and one bar with three of its four parts shaded appear
marks.sum: the mixed number three plus three fourths is written under them

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it uses bars.
<bookmark mark='bars'/>Three bars are whole, and one bar has three of its four parts shaded.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>That is the number three plus three fourths.
Can we write it as a regular fraction?

beats.on_screen: the bars and the mixed number stay; the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: each whole bar cut into four equal parts, each part labelled 1/4

marks.cut: each whole bar is cut into four equal parts
marks.fourth: each part is labelled one fourth

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>The last bar is cut into four equal parts, so every whole bar can be cut that way.
<bookmark mark='fourth'/>Each part is one fourth of a whole.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the number that we have to look at is three plus three fourths.

beats.on_screen: To find: 3 + 3/4 as a regular fraction
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write it as a regular fraction.

marks.split: the three is split into three separate wholes
marks.whole: each whole bar is split into four fourths and written as four times one fourth

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, three plus three fourths means one plus one plus one plus three fourths.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>Each whole is four fourths. That is four times one fourth.

marks.all: every whole is replaced by four times one fourth, and three fourths is written as three times one fourth

narration: <bookmark mark='all'/>Step three, write everything in fourths. Three wholes are three groups of four times one fourth, and then three times one fourth.

marks.add: the counts four, four, four and three are added to make fifteen fourths

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step four, add the counts of fourths. Four plus four plus four plus three is fifteen, so we have fifteen fourths.

marks.check: twelve fourths are grouped into three wholes and three fourths are left

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, take wholes out of fifteen fourths. Twelve fourths make three wholes, and three fourths are left.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Three plus three fourths is fifteen fourths.
Yes, a mixed number can be written as a regular fraction.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the bars
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says 3 + 3/4 is 6/4 because 3 and 3 make 6; the three whole bars are cut into fourths and counted as 12 fourths; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: the bubble with the wrong idea appears
marks.cut: the three whole bars are cut into fourths and twelve fourths are counted
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and the three left fourths are added to the twelve

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks three plus three fourths is six fourths, because three and three make six.
<bookmark mark='cut'/>Cut the three whole bars into fourths. Each whole gives four fourths, so three wholes give twelve fourths.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Then we add the three fourths that were already there.
